newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - New Holland profit margins, sales rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - New Holland profit margins, sales rise.

text.p: Agricultural equipment-maker New Holland said on Tuesday its operating profit margin rose slightly last year compared with 1995 as sales of tractors, combines and industrial equipment increased strongly.
New Holland, one of the world's largest agricultural and construction equipment makers, said provisional data showed group revenues totalled $5.5 billion last year, an increase of 11 percent on 1995.
The company, which was partially spun off from Italian industrial giant Fiat last year, said its consolidated operating profit margin rose to 8.9 percent from 8.2 percent in 1995.
It sold more than 85,700 tractors in 1996, 4.7 percent up on 1995, and nearly 4,700 combines, 17.7 percent more than in 1995. Construction and industrial equipment sales rose 15.6 percent.
Fourth quarter 1996 consolidated revenue climbed 36 percent on the 1995 fourth quarter to $1.4 billion. The company said, full results were due at the end of February.
Prospects for 1997 were positive, it said, with economic growth in its markets forecast to be similar to 1996.

"Farm income in both Europe and North America remains healthy and industry demand is generally expected to remain near 1996 levels with growth expected in Brazil, Latin America and Asia," a statement said.
Unit sales and revenues were forecast rising this year while sales should be boosted by full availability of new products launched last year and higher demand.

Demand for construction equipment in Europe remained at a low level "primarily because of tight government spending policies related to requirements for entry into European economic and monetary union".

But overall "based on favourable markets and anticipated demand for our products and the continued successful implementation of our global product and marketing strategies, we continue to remain positive in our outlook for the future," managing director Umberto Quadrino said in the statement.
New Holland is 69 percent owned by Dutch-registered New Holland NV, a subsidiary of Fiat, and began trading on Wall Street in November last year after a public share offering.
